## Errors

Each error carries `doc_url` pointing at its own entry in the error reference, and `request_id` — always a
string — matching the `X-Request-Id` response header. Quote it in support.

## Legacy top-level keys

Additive only, never a second contract: on error bodies the runtime still emits the pre-contract
top-level keys shipped clients read. `error_code` and `message` ride top-level on the refusals the platform
itself raises (including the storefront sign-in branches);
`request_id` and `doc_url` ride top-level ONLY on storefront, client, developer and dashboard error bodies
— the Merchant API reissues refusals, so there they live inside `error`.
They are documented separately under `QueekLegacyErrorKeys`, which no operation references. New integrations
switch on `error.*`.

## Request ids

Send `X-Request-Id` (8–128 chars matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$`) to correlate your trace with ours,
or read the one we generate — it is echoed on every response, error bodies included, and appears on every log line
of the request. `X-Queek-Api-Version` carries the API version (`v1`).

## Idempotency

Send `Idempotency-Key` on a write and a retry cannot execute twice. Same key + same body replays the stored
response verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` for 24h. Same key + a different body is
`409 idempotency_key_reuse`. A concurrent duplicate waits 15s for the first to finish, then replays;
past that it is `409 idempotency_key_in_progress`. Responses ≥ 400 are not stored, so a failure stays retryable.
The slot is vendor + caller + METHOD:path + key. The body is the fingerprint, not part of the slot. Operations that accept the header document it as a parameter.

## Rate limits

180 requests/min per API key + IP, or storefront origin + IP when no key is sent. On top of that, a private (`sk_live_`) key carries its
store's plan quota: `free` 60/min, `social_media` 120/min, `starter` 120/min, `growth` 240/min, `scale` 1200/min, `enterprise` 2400/min. sk_live_ private keys only. A pk_live_ public key is shared by every visitor of the store, so it gets no per-store bucket.
Exceeding either is `too_many_requests` with `Retry-After`.

## Webhooks

Subscribe an endpoint per store and Queek posts the signed event to it. Topics are listed under `webhooks`
in this document; the body is signed with the Standard Webhooks scheme — HMAC-SHA256 over the base64-decoded secret, value `v1,<base64>` —
over `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}`, tolerance 300s. A rotation keeps the previous secret valid for
24h and sends both signatures, space delimited. Delivery is 8 attempts on a published backoff;
an endpoint failing for 24h is disabled and the merchant notified. Every operation names the one scope it requires. A write scope also returns, in that write's own response, the record it wrote — listing or reading records needs the matching read scope. A key acts for its whole store, never only for the records one person created. Additive-only under v1: new operations, fields and enum values may be added, but existing operations, fields, values and auth behaviour never change incompatibly. A breaking change ships as v2 alongside v1, never in place.

## Money

Every amount you read is a major-unit decimal string at the currency's own precision (`"1500.00"`; UGX `"1500"`; KWD `"1.250"`), never a JSON number. Each object that carries an amount also carries its `currency` code (ISO-4217), or sits inside an object that does; the API sends no preformatted display text (no `*_text`), so format from `amount` + `currency`. Discount and coupon values of the percentage type are percentages with two decimals (`"12.50"`), not amounts.

Amounts you send are major units too, as a decimal string or a number: `"1500.50"` and `1500.5` are equivalent. A request is refused with `422` when an amount has more decimals than the store currency allows, is negative where a minimum applies, or exceeds the maximum the field can store; the error names the field.

## Dates

Every `*_at` field is an ISO-8601 timestamp with numeric offset (`format: date-time`), written on the platform clock (Africa/Lagos, `+01:00`): one instant has one spelling in every store. The store object's `timezone` is the zone to render it in.

Every day-based input or read follows the store's own calendar in that `timezone`: analytics `start_date`/`end_date`, order `from_date`/`to_date`/`date_range`, and "today". A date-time you send without an offset (a coupon's `starts_at`, a discount's `valid_until`, a post's `published_at`) is read on the store's clock; one with an offset keeps it.

## Deletes and creates

DELETE answers `200` with the envelope (`{status, message, data}`), never `204`. Existing creates answer `200` and new creates answer `201` — both statuses are documented per operation and neither will change under you.

get.description:
Requires scope `merchant-options-read`.

Lists this store’s add-on groups with cursor pagination (`limit` + `starting_after`, `has_more`/`next_cursor`; at most 25 per page). Each group carries at most 20 items with `items_count`/`items_truncated` beside them — read the group itself for the full member list before patching it. Only the store’s own groups ever list: a shared group is attach-only by ref and never appears here.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of items to return in one page.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Cursor for the next page: pass `next_cursor` from the previous response unchanged. Keep walking while `has_more` is true.

parameters.name: X-Client-Key
parameters.description: A private API key (`sk_live_…`, `sk_test_…` on a dev store) minted by a Server connection under Dashboard → Channels → Headless API (keys are also listed in Settings → Connections). The key is bound to ONE store, so no vendor header or `vendor_id` is sent; its scopes decide which operations it may call. `pk_` public keys never reach this API. Keep it on your server.

get.description:
Requires scope `merchant-analytics-traffic-read`.

Reads up to 30 days of anonymous storefront traffic for this store: daily views and visits, bot request count, and measurement metadata. Visits are not unique visitors because shared mobile networks can group shoppers. Bot requests count requests and are not views. Figures can lag live traffic by up to about ten minutes (daily totals refresh every five minutes and responses are cached for up to five); only the installed app's own key with this grant can use this route.

get.description:
Requires scope `merchant-analytics-sales-read`.

Reads the store’s sales for a range of whole days: order counts, gross revenue and average order value of completed orders, daily, weekly or monthly order and revenue trends (daily up to 31 days, weekly up to 90), and orders by status and by sales channel. `start_date` and `end_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, both or neither) default to the last 30 days; a range may be at most 90 days and may not end after today (422 otherwise). Amounts are decimal strings in the store currency. Net revenue, fees and settlements are payments data and are not included. Figures are computed from the store’s orders, cached for up to three minutes and shared by every app of the store, so they can lag a new order by that long. Requires scope `merchant-collected-records-submit`.

Submits one record under one of the calling installation’s collected types. Values run the same field validation entries use; every record is filed with source `app`. Send an `Idempotency-Key` to make a retry safe: the same key and body replays the first answer instead of filing the record twice, the same key with a different body is 409; the header is optional. Creates are capped per installation at 30 a minute and 2000 a day (429 + Retry-After past either), on top of the per-definition storage cap of 5000 records. This is a form-submission path, not a bulk store: keep many small items inside one record’s values (up to 64 KiB) instead of one record each. put.description:
Requires scope `merchant-collections-update`.

Replaces a collection’s fields; `name` is required. Renaming never changes the collection’s URL: `slug` is the URL handle (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 100, unique in the store), send it only to change the address, and the old address then redirects to the new one automatically. `seo` is the search listing, `{title, description}` (plain text, up to 255 and 1000 characters): leave the key out to keep it, send an object to replace it, send null or blank values to clear it; the storefront then falls back to the name and the description. `metafields` is a list of `{namespace, key, value}` checked against the store’s `collection` definitions: a `null` value clears one, a key left out keeps its value, and an undefined handle answers 422. Answers the updated collection — the same object GET collections/{collection} returns.

At most 50 sections and 256 KB.

Requires scope `merchant-conversations-read`.

Lists the store’s messaging conversations (WhatsApp, Instagram and Telegram), newest first by creation, with cursor pagination (`limit` up to 50 + `starting_after`, `has_more`/`next_cursor`). `status` defaults to `active`; `channel` narrows to one line. Previews and message text are written by shoppers and can contain anything they typed, contact details included. Requires a store plan that includes the messaging inbox; without it the answer is the same 403 the dashboard gives. Whether the AI or the team answers cannot be changed through this API.

post.description:
Requires scope `merchant-conversations-reply`.

Sends a reply to the shopper on the conversation’s own line (the store’s WhatsApp, Instagram or Telegram) and stores it on the thread, marked as sent by this app (the team sees `sender_name` "<app name> (app)"). `type` is `text` (`content` required), `image` (`image_url` required, `content` an optional caption) or `product` (`product_id`, a product of this store that is published, with `product_format` `card` or `link`); button messages are not available to apps. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: it is required, and a retry with the same key and body replays the first answer instead of messaging the shopper twice. On WhatsApp and Instagram a free-form reply is allowed only within 24 hours of the shopper’s last message: after that the answer is 409 `messaging_window_closed` and nothing is sent. Telegram has no window. Replying pauses the store’s AI on this conversation for the store’s takeover window, as a dashboard reply does; the answer carries `mode` and `mode_expires_at`. If the channel refuses the message the answer is 424 `channel_gateway_unreachable`, nothing is stored, and the same request can be retried. Each installation may send 20 replies a minute and 1,000 a day (429 with Retry-After beyond that). Requires a store plan that includes the messaging inbox.

get.description:
Requires scope `merchant-customers-read`.

Lists customers with cursor pagination (`limit` up to 100 + `starting_after`, `has_more`/`next_cursor`); profile fields match customers/* webhooks and email_marketing_consent and sms_marketing_consent are present only with merchant-customers-contact-read. Use audience=campaign to include non-buyers; that mode requires the contact scope. not_opted_out means only that the person has not used Queek’s email unsubscribe; it is not permission to send. An import that stores info.marketing_opt_in=false excludes that contact from campaign reachability. Optional `updated_after` walks customer rows changed after a timestamp, oldest change first, by each customer’s `updated_at` (second precision); start each poll five minutes before the previous poll start, deduplicate ids, keep filters fixed and walk sequentially. With `updated_after`, `sort_by`, `sort_order`, `page` and `per_page` return 422; a cursor is bound to the same timestamp and filters. Changes stored outside the customer record (order history, consent changes recorded elsewhere) and deleted customers may be missed. The filter time is not returned; this is not a snapshot or deletion feed.

Records explicit app-reported SMS marketing consent for this customer. state=subscribed requires source, opt_in_level, consent_updated_at, and a valid phone number; state=unsubscribed needs no evidence fields or phone. Requires scope `merchant-purchase_orders-update`.

Receives goods against a purchase order, in full or in part: each `items[]` line (at most 100) names a `purchase_order_item` (a line `id`) and a `quantity_received` (1 to 1,000,000), plus the `variant` (its p_id) the goods are for; a line for a product with active variants must name one (else 422 `variant_required`, nothing received), and a variant that is not of that line’s product in this store is a 422. The quantity is added to that variant’s stock (the product’s totals follow), or, for a product without variants, to the product’s stock, with a stock adjustment linked to the receipt, and the receipt records the line’s ordered `unit_cost`; the product’s own cost price is not changed. The order becomes `partial` or `received`; receiving a `draft` marks it ordered first. An `Idempotency-Key` header is REQUIRED: a retry with the same key and body replays the first answer instead of receiving the goods twice, and a different body under a used key answers 409. A cancelled, closed or fully received order answers 409 `conflict`; a line that would take in more than it has left answers 422, and nothing is received at all when any line is refused; 422s name the line (`items.{index}.variant` or `items.{index}.quantity_received` in `error.errors`). Each received line writes a stock adjustment of type `purchase_order_received` (positive `quantity_change`, variant scope when a variant was named, `reason_code` null), readable at GET inventory/adjustments?type=purchase_order_received. A purchase order or line that is not in this store answers 404. Answers the purchase order with its receipts.

get.description:
Requires scope `merchant-invoices-read`.

Lists the store’s invoices, newest first, with cursor pagination (`limit` + `starting_after`, `has_more`/`next_cursor`). Needs the Invoices app installed on the store (403 `app_not_installed` otherwise). Every row is the object GET invoices/{invoice} answers: `number` (null on a draft), `kind` (`invoice`, `proforma` or `credit_note`), `status` (`overdue` is derived: issued, past its due date, balance left), `source` (`standalone`, or `order` for an invoice that mirrors an order’s payments and balance, with that `order`), the `buyer`, the `lines`, the totals, `payments`, `installments` and `credit_notes`. Every id is a p_id, every amount a decimal string at the invoice’s currency precision beside its ISO `currency`. Filters: `status`, `kind`, `customer_id` and `order_id` (a p_id or UUID of this store; one that is not this store’s lists nothing), `q` (number, title or buyer name or phone; needs merchant-customers-contact-read, 403 `insufficient_scope` without it), `from` and `to` (creation dates, Y-m-d) and `updated_since` (RFC 3339 with an explicit offset: keeps rows changed at or after that time). The buyer’s `name`, `email` and `phone` are null without merchant-customers-contact-read; the address and tax id are on the document either way. An order-backed invoice (`source` `order`) follows its order only when it is read: the `updated_since` and `status` filters run on the stored row, so they do not see an order payment until the invoice is read (a row can list under its old `status` and a stale `updated_at`); watch the `orders/*` webhooks or read GET orders/{order}/invoice instead, and note that reading refreshes it and moves its `updated_at`. The customer link, the order’s pay link, customer payment notices and the merchant’s bank details are never in the object. The window moves as rows change, so a walk through pages is not a snapshot: poll with `updated_since` for invoices the merchant makes and deduplicate on `id` and `updated_at`.

Requires scope `merchant-invoices-create`.

Creates a DRAFT invoice (or a `proforma`, which is not a tax invoice): it has no `number` yet and is not shown to the customer until it is issued with POST invoices/{invoice}/issue. You send only what a person would type: `lines` (`description`, `quantity`, `unit_price` and optionally `tax_rate`, `tax_name` or several named `taxes`), the `buyer` (`name`, `email`, `phone`, `address`, `tax_id`) or a `customer_id` (a p_id or UUID of one of this store’s customers, whose details fill the buyer), an invoice-level `discount` (`type` `fixed` or `percent`, `value`), `due_at`, `terms`, `note`, `title`, `language` (`en`, `fr` or `ar`) and an `installments` plan. The server computes every total: the subtotal, discount, tax and total are never accepted, and a `total_amount`, line total or tax amount you send is ignored. Money is a decimal string in the invoice’s `currency` (the store’s currency unless you send a supported `currency`), with no more decimals than that currency has (more answers 422). Answers 201 with the invoice as GET invoices/{invoice} reads it. Needs the Invoices app installed on the store (403 `app_not_installed` otherwise). A draft is not a document yet: it takes no payment and consumes no invoice number. Fires `invoices/create`. Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a retried call does not create a second draft.

Needs the Invoices app installed on the store (403 `app_not_installed` otherwise). Fires `invoices/create` when it makes the invoice.

post.description:
Requires scope `merchant-invoices-record-payment`.

Records money the merchant confirmed receiving against an issued invoice: a bank transfer, cash, a card terminal, mobile money, or tax withheld at source (`method`: `bank_transfer`, `cash`, `pos`, `mobile_money`, `other` or `tax_withheld`). Nothing moves through Queek: it settles the document only, and never reaches the store’s wallet or payouts. `amount` is a decimal string in the invoice’s `currency` with no more decimals than it has, above zero and not above the balance (`amount_due`): a larger one answers 409 `invoice_state_conflict`. The invoice’s `amount_paid`, `amount_due`, `status` and instalments follow the payments. A draft, a void invoice, one already paid in full, a proforma, a credit note, a credited invoice and an order-backed invoice (`source` `order`: its payments are the order’s own) answer 409. `paid_at` may not be in the future; `reference` is the payer’s or the bank’s reference. `Idempotency-Key` is required (400 `idempotency_key_required` without it): the same key replays the first answer without recording a second payment, and the same key with another amount, method, date or reference answers 409 `idempotency_key_reuse`, however long ago the first call was. A key is yours alone: another key or installation sending the same string records its own payment. {invoice} is a p_id or UUID of this store. Answers 201 with the invoice as GET invoices/{invoice} reads it. Needs the Invoices app installed on the store (403 `app_not_installed` otherwise). Fires `invoices/update`.

post.description:
Requires scope `merchant-metafields-create`.

Creates a metafield definition. An installed app that creates one in its own `app_{slug}` namespace (the slug with hyphens as underscores, exactly: `app_{slug}_…` is another app’s) owns it: the definition is hidden from the storefront unless `storefront_visible` is true, `merchant_access` is `read` (the merchant sees the values, the app alone writes them) or `read_write`, and only that app reads or writes its values through the API (another app and a plain store key cannot). Any other namespace creates the merchant’s own definition, exactly as before; the `app` and `app_…` namespace form is reserved for apps and refused to anyone else. `merchant_access` is refused on a definition that is not app-owned. Uninstalling the app hands its definitions and values to the merchant. `owner_type` `installation` is an app’s own data on its installation (read and written with GET and PATCH app/metafields): only an installed app creates one, in its own `app_{slug}` namespace, without `storefront_visible` or `merchant_access`; at most 50 per installation, outside the store’s definition limit; they are deleted, not handed over, at uninstall.

get.description:
Requires scope `merchant-orders-read`.

Lists the store’s orders using the same base object as orders/* webhooks; recorded payment transactions and Queek wallet-refund rows are present only with merchant-orders-read (webhooks include them only for active installations granted that scope). Order status, shipment, import, rider-assignment and patch responses do not include those finance arrays. Same filtering and search as the dashboard table with cursor pagination (`limit` + `starting_after`, `has_more`/`next_cursor`). `from_date` and `to_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, whole days) or `date_range` (`today`, `this_week`, `this_month`) keep orders created in a window, counted on the store’s own calendar (its `timezone`). `status=open` keeps orders that are not cancelled, rejected or completed; `payment_status=outstanding` keeps orders with money still owed (stored `pending`, `unpaid`, `partially_paid` or `awaiting_confirmation`) that are not cancelled or rejected; every stored payment word still filters on its exact value. `payment_method` is one stored method, or `offline_all` (offline, pos, bank_transfer, or an offline payment mode) / `online_all` (every other order that has a method). Each line item carries `variant_id` (the variant’s `id`), `variant_uid` and `sku`, so sales per variant need no match on `variant_title`. `publication` scopes the list to one of the calling installation’s channel publications (p_id or key; human keys use p_id and need the publications-read permission, without it the filter answers 404). `custom_channel` scopes the list to one hand-recorded or third-party channel name (for example `physical_sale` or `others`) and combines with the other filters. Optional `updated_after` walks order rows changed after a timestamp, oldest change first; start each poll five minutes before the previous poll start, deduplicate ids, keep filters fixed and walk sequentially. With `updated_after`, `sort_by`, `sort_order`, `page` and `per_page` return 422; a cursor is bound to the same timestamp and filters. Item/property, shipment, metafield or customer-profile changes and deleted orders may be missed; long-running changes may appear late. The filter time is not returned and may differ from `updated_at`; this is not a snapshot or deletion feed. Provider-side, vendor-collected, offline and manual-review refunds without a recorded Queek refund row are omitted.

post.description:
Requires scope `merchant-orders-create`.

Creates an order for this store, awaiting payment, and answers the order object orders/* webhooks send. Each line names its `product` (p_id, UUID or slug of this store), a `variant` when the product has variants (p_id or UUID of one of that product’s variants), a `quantity` and optional `addons` (option item p_id or UUID of that product). No price is ever sent: the order engine the dashboard uses prices every line, adds delivery and tax, and applies the optional `discount_amount`, a store-funded amount that is refused when it would leave nothing to charge. `delivery_method` is `instore`, `pickup` or `delivery`; delivery needs `delivery_address`, `map_lat` and `map_lng`. `payment_method` is `bank_transfer` (instore or pickup; the order waits as `awaiting_confirmation` until payment is approved with orders/{order}/status) or `online` (any delivery method; needs a `customer` with an account; the order waits as `pending` for the customer’s payment). An order is never created paid, and cash, wallet and split payments are not offered. `customer` is optional: name one customer of this store by exactly one of `id` (customer id, uid or user id), `email` or `phone`; email and phone lookups need merchant-customers-contact-read; without a customer the order is recorded for a guest. The order is attributed to the calling app (platform `custom`, channel `others`, labelled with the app name), carries no platform commission, and sends no new-order alert and no customer email. Stock is checked now and taken when the order completes, as for every order. Send an Idempotency-Key header: without one, a retried request creates a second order. No payment link is returned and no draft is kept: an unpaid order is a real order that stays open, holding no stock, until it is paid or cancelled; nothing expires it automatically. Metafields and metadata are written afterwards with PATCH orders/{order}.

get.description:
Requires scope `merchant-checkouts-read`.

Lists the store’s abandoned checkouts, newest first, with cursor pagination (`limit` + `starting_after`, `has_more`/`next_cursor`). `stage` picks the kind: `cart` (the default) is signed-in customers of this store whose cart has been unchanged for the idle delay (60 minutes by default) and is no older than the maximum age (72 hours by default); `payment` is unpaid checkouts, orders a signed-in customer placed and never paid, left unpaid for the unpaid-checkout delay (2 hours by default) and no older than the maximum age, and also needs the merchant-checkouts-payments-read scope (403 without it). Each stage is its own list with its own cursor, and a row is keyed by `stage` plus `id`: a cart and an order can share an `id`. A customer is reported at most once per stage, by their latest cart or latest unpaid order. A cart is dropped once the customer placed an order at this store after its last change; an unpaid order is dropped once they placed an order, or started another order that was not cancelled, after it. Guest carts and orders, orders made on the Queek marketplace (the store dashboard lists those under abandoned orders), orders sent as a staff payment link, orders with a payment under review, empty carts and carts last changed before this feature started are not listed. `include_completed=true` (payment only) also lists recovered checkouts: orders paid at least the idle delay after they were created, with `completed_at` set; a refunded one stays listed, and it is off by default so a recovery app never messages someone who already paid. Each row has `id`, `stage`, `created_at`, `updated_at` (a cart’s last change; a payment row’s paid-or-created time, which does not move when the shopper opens the pay page), `completed_at`, the `customer` (`id`; `name`, `email` and `phone` are null without merchant-customers-contact-read), `line_items` (`product` and `variant` ids, the store’s own `title`, `quantity`; no prices) and `checkout_url`, the store’s checkout page, the same link for every shopper (the shopper signs in to see their cart). Four more keys are null on a cart: `order` (`id`, which opens orders/{order}, and `order_number`), `currency` (the store’s currency, never a shopper’s presentment currency), `total` (the order total as a decimal string, the same number as orders/{order}) and `recovery_url`, the order’s payment page, present only for an `online` order that can still be paid. The link does not expire and cannot be revoked, except that it is null for an order in a market whose exchange rate has expired (the shopper places the order again): treat it as a secret, never log it or pass it to a third party. A cart row is the object the checkouts/create and checkouts/update webhooks send, which carry carts only and need merchant-checkouts-read; a payment row is the object the payment_checkouts/create webhook sends once per unpaid order, which needs both merchant-checkouts-read and merchant-checkouts-payments-read (there is no update event: a recovered checkout is the orders/create webhook for the same order id; sent once per unpaid checkout in normal operation; a delivery can occasionally be missed (infrastructure failure after the checkout is claimed) or arrive twice (retries): deduplicate by (topic, order id), and use GET abandoned-checkouts?stage=payment to reconcile). `updated_since` (RFC 3339 with an explicit offset) keeps rows changed at or after that time. A cart counts as abandoned when it is unchanged, not when the shopper is inactive. The window moves with the clock and rows change, so a walk through pages is not a snapshot: poll with `updated_since` and deduplicate on `stage`, `id` and `updated_at`. A customer who buys after a cart is detected with orders/create.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of items to return in one page.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Cursor for the next page: pass `next_cursor` from the previous response unchanged. Keep walking while `has_more` is true.

parameters.name: stage

post.description:
Requires scope `merchant-orders-import`.

Records an order already charged by an outside platform: each item names its `product` (p_id, UUID or slug of this store) and, for a variant, its `variant` (p_id or UUID of a variant belonging to that product) — the old single `ref` is refused; totals are stored as charged with no commission, and a re-sent order returns the same record. The authenticated app installation supplies source attribution; only an installed legacy marketplace app sends `channel`, and it must match its own app slug; any other app omits it, and a supplied value is rejected. The customer (name + phone) becomes the order’s `shipping_address` recipient, readable only with merchant-customers-contact-read like every contact — never `metadata`. `delivery_fee` and `discount` are required: send "0.00" when there is none, and `total` must equal the lines plus `delivery_fee` minus `discount`. `placed_at` is when the outside platform took the order: on a dev store it becomes the order’s `created_at` (the order’s `updated_at` is still the import time), so a developer can build sales history, and it must be within the last 120 days, the time a dev store keeps imported orders (older answers 422); on a live store the order is recorded now and `placed_at` is kept as its order date. Answers the order object orders/* webhooks send. Generic app installations derive source from the authenticated installation and omit `channel`; supplying it is a 422. An installed legacy marketplace app must send the `channel` slug matching its own app slug; mismatches are 422. Human-key legacy imports still require `channel` and may choose either slug. Those slugs are not reserved.

post.description:
Requires scope `merchant-orders-refund-create`.

Refunds part or all of what a customer paid for an order, against ONE payment of the order: `payment` names it (a payment `id` from the order's `transactions`), else the newest received payment with something left. The refund follows the original payment and the caller never chooses where it goes: a payment Queek collected through its provider goes back to the customer through that provider (it starts `pending` and ends `success` or `failed`), a payment from the customer's Queek wallet goes back to the wallet, and a payment the store collected on its own gateway or took offline is only RECORDED: Queek moves no money and the store refunds the customer itself. `amount` is always sent (a decimal string in the order currency) and may not exceed what is left to refund on that payment and on the order; a refund cannot be undone. `line_items` (`order_item`: a line `id` from the order, `quantity`, `restock`) tell Queek which lines were refunded and put tracked stock back on the shelf; they never set the amount. `Idempotency-Key` is required: the same key with the same body returns the refund already made (200), the same key with another body is 409. `notify` (default true) tells the customer when the refund lands; `note` is for the store only and is never sent to the customer or in a webhook. Fires `refunds/create` when the refund is created and `orders/updated` when a provider refund finishes or fails. Answers 201 with the refund, `refundable` and `restocked`.

Requires scope `merchant-items-read`.

Lists the store’s products — the same object products/* webhooks send, with variants, images, the canonical URL and the storefront price. Same filtering as the dashboard table with cursor pagination (`limit` + `starting_after`, `has_more`/`next_cursor`); sorts limited to public fields. Optional `updated_after` walks product rows changed after a timestamp, oldest change first; start each poll five minutes before the previous poll start, deduplicate ids, keep filters fixed and walk sequentially. With `updated_after`, `sort_by`, `sort_order`, `page` and `per_page` return 422; a cursor is bound to the same timestamp and filters. Variant, image, metafield, stock, region, price, discount, bulk publish, unpublish, archive status or inventory-tracking changes and deleted products may be missed; long-running changes may appear late. The filter time is not returned and may differ from `updated_at`; this is not a snapshot or deletion feed. `publication` scopes the list to one of the calling installation channel publications (p_id or key; human keys use p_id and need the publications-read permission, without it the filter answers 404): with `updated_after` it returns additions and content changes, while a removed product surfaces only in the full reconcile walk, never as a delta. `cost_price` (the unit cost, a money string or null when none was ever set) is present, on the product and on each variant, only with the protected merchant-items-cost-read scope. A variant has its own cost and a variant without one reads null, never the product’s. Older products had an unset cost filled with the selling price and still read it: a cost equal to the price on an old product is unknown, not a fact.

patch.description:
Requires scope `merchant-metafields-update`.

Writes metafield values on one product without resending the product: `metafields` is a list of `{namespace, key, value}`. Each handle needs a product metafield definition (create it with POST metafield-definitions first), values are type-checked, a handle you leave out keeps its value and `"value": null` deletes one. The platform namespaces `app.*` and `queek.*` are refused; an app-owned definition’s values (its `app_{slug}` namespace, see POST metafield-definitions) are written only by that app. Answers the updated product — the same object GET products/{product} sends; storefront-hidden merchant values appear in it only with merchant-metafields-read, and an app always reads its own app-owned values. Variant values have their own route, PATCH products/{product}/variants/{variant}/metafields, under the same scope. Does not move `updated_at`; sends one products/update webhook.

post.description:
Requires scope `merchant-exports-create`.

Queues a whole-store archive (a zip of CSV files plus `manifest.json`) and answers 202 with the export row. It is always built in the background; read `exports/{export}` until `status` is `ready` and the `download_url` appears. The archive carries only what this key can read: `products.csv` needs merchant-items-read, `orders.csv` needs merchant-orders-read and `customers.csv` needs merchant-customers-read; a key holding none of them answers 422. Without merchant-customers-contact-read the customer and buyer name, email and phone cells are blank. `manifest.json` lists exactly what the archive carries. The archive is customer personal data and `download_url` is a bearer link: anyone holding it can download the archive until `expires_at`, so keep it out of logs and share it with nobody. One export runs per store at a time (409 `export_in_progress` while one is active, including one the merchant started in the dashboard), and an installation may request three per rolling 24 hours (429 with `Retry-After`). A key reads only the exports it requested. The archive is a snapshot at build time and has no deletion feed: records removed since a previous export are simply absent, so reconcile by comparing archives.

post.description:
Requires scope `merchant-taxes-create`.

Creates a tax row. `rate_percent` is a percentage from 0 to 100 with at most two decimals (a string or a number). `channel` defaults to `all`. A store keeps one active tax per channel: creating an active tax switches off the store’s other active tax of the same channel, so create a second rate only when it should replace the first. A `name` already used in the channel, by a switched-off tax too, answers 422: bring that tax back with `active: true` on its update instead. There is no delete: switch a tax off with `active: false`. Taxes are added on top of prices (never included in them) and the rate is not checked against any country’s rules: the merchant is responsible for it. Answers 201 with the tax. Changing a tax changes what shoppers are charged at their next checkout, so only write what the merchant asked for. `Idempotency-Key` is optional and makes a retried create replay the first answer.

post.description:
Requires scope `merchant-translations-machine`.

Prices a machine translation job before anything runs. The body is a REFERENCE, never text: the target `locale` (a language the store has enabled), a `mode` (`missing`, `outdated` or `missing_and_outdated`; the outdated modes refresh machine translations only) and `resources` (`type`, `id`, optional `keys`) naming the store's own content, which is read from the store in its primary language. Answers a `quote_id` good for ten minutes, the `texts` and source `characters` it covers, the `estimated_credits` (an upper bound: the run never charges more) and the `held` keys that will not be translated (a store policy page is translated by hand). Charges nothing. The store must have the credits and the merchant must have left the app's machine translation switch on; a job is limited to 200,000 characters, 20 resources and 20 keys per resource, and a store to 1,000,000 characters a day. A job runs inside a time budget: once it is spent the remaining texts are `held` as `time_budget` and the app runs the rest again.

Runs a quoted machine translation job: send the `quote_id` with the same `locale`, `mode` and `resources` it priced. id.description: The cart's or the order's `p_id`; with `stage` it is the row's key.

created_at.description: When this object was created (ISO-8601 timestamp).

updated_at.description: A cart: its last change. A payment row: when the order was placed (paid), else when it was created; never the order's own `updated_at`, which moves when the pay page is opened.

checkout_url.description: The store's checkout page, the same link for every shopper.

stage.description: `cart`: a signed-in customer's idle cart. `payment`: an unpaid checkout (an order whose payment never arrived), on the list for a key holding `merchant-checkouts-payments-read`, and in `payment_checkouts/create`.

completed_at.description: When the checkout was recovered: the time the order was placed (paid) after being left. Null while it is still unpaid, and always null on a cart.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code of the store's currency, the one `total` is in.

total.description: The order total as a decimal string in the store's currency (not a shopper's presentment currency); null on a cart, which has no authoritative price.

recovery_url.description: A payment link for the shopper: the order's pay page, present only for an `online` order that can still be paid. It does not expire and cannot be revoked, except that it is null for an order in a market whose exchange rate has expired (the shopper places the order again): treat it as a secret (never log it, never pass it to a third party). so a retry replays and removals are explicit (an empty `items` removes every

CreateMerchantOrderRequest.description:
POST orders on the Merchant API: an order the store's own app or key rings up
for a customer, created awaiting payment.

The body names WHAT is sold, never what it costs: every product, variant and
add-on is a reference resolved inside the key's store, and every amount is
computed by the same order engine the dashboard uses. Fields that would let a
caller dictate money, state or origin (a total, a status, a payment status, a
platform) are refused by name rather than ignored, so a caller that sends one
learns it now.

line_items.description: What is sold, one entry per line (1 to 100). Never a price: the order engine prices every line.

product.description: The product: a p_id, UUID or slug of a product of this store. A product of another store answers 404 unknown_product_ref.

variant.description: The variant, a p_id or UUID of one of THAT product's variants. Required when the product has variants.

quantity.description: How many, 1 to 1000. Stock is checked now and taken when the order completes.

addons.description: Add-on option items for the line: a p_id or UUID of an option item of THAT product.

customer.description: Optional. One customer of this store, named by exactly one of `id`, `email` or `phone`. Without a customer the order is recorded for a guest.

id.description: The customer id: the public customer id, its uid, or the person's user id, resolved inside this store.

email.description: The customer's email. Needs the merchant-customers-contact-read scope.

phone.description: The customer's phone, with or without the country code. Needs the merchant-customers-contact-read scope.

sell_anyway.description: Optional. In a store with several locations the order is routed to one that can cover it, else the one holding the most, and marked short there. Send `false` to be refused instead when the location is short, `true` to sell anyway. Left out, the order is created.

sell_anyway_reason.description: Optional. Why the order was sold short, kept with it (200 characters).

delivery_method.description: `instore`, `pickup` or `delivery`. Delivery orders are paid online.

delivery_address.description: Where to deliver. Needed with map_lat and map_lng when a line ships something.

payment_method.description: `bank_transfer` (instore or pickup; waits as awaiting_confirmation) or `online` (any delivery method; needs a customer with an account; waits as pending). An order is never created paid.

discount_amount.description: Optional store-funded discount in the store's currency, a decimal string with at most 2 decimals. Refused when it would leave nothing to charge.

coupon_code.description: Optional. One of the store's discount codes, in any case, applied to this order's lines for its customer. Refused with the code's own reason when it does not apply; not allowed together with `discount_amount`.

note.description: An internal note kept on the order (up to 2000 characters).

What an order imported through POST orders/import does to stock (the request's `inventory_behavior`). An import is an order the outside platform already took, so by default it claims nothing: a historical or already-fulfilled order must never hold or take today's stock. | | |---| | `bypass`
Claims no stock now or at completion; writes no stock row. The default. | | `decrement`
Takes the stock at import with a `sale` row, obeying the store's tracking and shortfall policy (a short line under `block` refuses the import). Completion takes nothing more; a cancel or refund restocks it like any order's sale. | | `reserve`
Like a Queek order: holds the stock while the order is open and takes it with a `sale` row when the order completes. For a live order the store still fulfils. |

ImportThirdPartyOrderRequest.description:
Import an order an outside sales channel already charged for. Generic app
source attribution comes from the authenticated installation.

The payload is the platform's receipt, recorded as charged. Item unit
prices, delivery fee, discount and total are amounts in naira with at most
2 decimals (6500 or "6500.00"), like every Merchant API amount, and they
must add up: the sum of unit_price × quantity, plus delivery_fee, minus
discount, equals total. Each item names its `product` (p_id, UUID or slug
of a product in this store)
and, for a variant, its `variant` (p_id or UUID of one of THAT product's
variants). The old single `ref` is refused: product and variant p_ids are
separate sequences, so one number could name two rows. A product from
another store fails the import with a named 422, never a cross-store sale.

The customer travels as name + phone only and becomes the order's
`shipping_address` recipient; no customer record is created.

channel.description: Optional for generic app installations, which derive source from the authenticated app and must omit this field. An installed legacy marketplace app must send its matching slug. A generic app supplying this field, or a legacy app sending the other slug, receives 422. Human-key legacy imports still require this field and may send either slug.

publication.description:
Optional attribution to one of the calling installation's active
publications (p_id or key). Omitted means no attribution. A
caller without an installation may not send it (422).

placed_at.description: When the outside platform took the order (RFC 3339). On a dev store it becomes the order's `created_at`, so history can be built for testing; it must fall within the dev-store import retention window (422 beyond it). On a live store the order is recorded now and this is kept as its order date. This field is an INPUT (the outside platform's order date): the `placed_at` in the order object the API returns is a different fact, the moment Queek placed the order, which equals this value only on a dev store.

ref.description:
The old single `ref` resolved variant-first, then product, across
two separate p_id sequences — one integer could name two rows.
Refused outright (never aliased): the caller must say which.

unit_price.description:
Naira, at most 2 decimals — the Merchant API's one money rule,
as for shipping-zone rates: a kobo figure is off by 100x and
runs past these caps instead of posing as naira.

delivery_fee.description: Required: send "0.00" when the order has no delivery fee.

discount.description: Required: send "0.00" when the order has no discount.

anyOf.description:
What the import does to stock. `bypass` (the default): claims none, now or at completion, and writes no stock row, for an order the outside platform already took and fulfilled. `decrement`: takes the stock now with a `sale` row on the stock adjustments, obeying the store's stock tracking and shortfall policy (under `block` a line short of stock refuses the whole import with 409 `conflict`, `data.reason` `insufficient_stock`; stock never goes below zero); completion then takes nothing more, and a cancel or refund restocks it. `reserve`: like an order placed in Queek, the open order holds the stock (`reserved` on the inventory lists) and takes it with a `sale` row when it completes; for a live order the store still fulfils. A store that does not track stock moves none in any mode. The response's `meta.inventory_behavior` says which one the order was imported with. A re-send with the same Idempotency-Key and a changed body answers 409 `idempotency_key_reuse`; a re-send without a key, or after the key expired (24 hours), returns the first order unchanged (200) with the first import's `meta.inventory_behavior`, whatever this says. | | |---| | `bypass`
Claims no stock now or at completion; writes no stock row. The default. | | `decrement`
Takes the stock at import with a `sale` row, obeying the store's tracking and shortfall policy (a short line under `block` refuses the import). Completion takes nothing more; a cancel or refund restocks it like any order's sale. | | `reserve`
Like a Queek order: holds the stock while the order is open and takes it with a `sale` row when the order completes. For a live order the store still fulfils. |

name.description: The market's name, unique within the store.

countries.description: The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of the countries the market sells to; a country belongs to one market of the store.

published.description: Whether the merchant has published the market: publishing is refused unless a provider can charge its currency and a current exchange rate exists.

status.description: `draft` (not published: shoppers cannot see it), `live` (published, and shoppers can pick it and pay in its currency right now) or `not_live` (published, but a blocker stops shoppers from using it, so they still see the store currency). Empty when nothing blocks. On a draft it lists what would refuse a publish. A snapshot of the moment of the read.

checkout_currency.description: The store's own currency, whatever the market's `currency`: the currency its prices and orders are kept in, and the one every order outside a published market is charged in. An order placed through a published market is charged in that market's `currency`.

is this store's p_id, UUID or slug; the detach {group} must already hang on

MerchantProductMetafieldsRequest.description:
Metafield values of one product, or of one of its variants
(products/{product}/variants/{variant}/metafields), and nothing else, so an app
never resends (or overwrites) the rest of the product, and never needs the broad
item-update scope, to change its own fields. Each handle must have a definition
for that owner type and its value is type-checked; a handle you leave out keeps
its value and `"value": null` deletes one. The platform's dotted namespaces
(`app.*`, `queek.*`) are refused; an app-owned `app_{slug}` value is written only
by its app (MetafieldAccess). Any other field is rejected by name rather than ignored.

MerchantReceivePurchaseOrderRequest.description:
POST purchase-orders/{po}/receive: the dashboard's request, gate
and rules (`merchant-purchase_orders-update`), naming each line the way the
rest of the Merchant API does (`items[].purchase_order_item`, the line `id`),
plus one rule of its own: receiving moves stock, so an `Idempotency-Key`
header is REQUIRED. A retry with the same key and body replays the first
answer instead of receiving the goods twice; a different body under a used
key is the standard 409.

A line may name the `variant` (its p_id) the goods are for: the quantity is then
added to that variant of the line's product and the product's totals follow.
A line for a product with active variants that names none is refused 422
`variant_required` and nothing is received.

purchase_order_item.description: The `id` of an order line of this purchase order.

variant.description: The `p_id` of the variant of the line's product the goods are for. Required when the product has active variants (else 422 `variant_required`); omit it for a product without variants. A variant that is not of that product in this store is a 422.

quantity_received.description: Units received, 1 to 1,000,000, at most what the line has left. Added to the named variant, else to the product's stock.

received_at.description: When the goods arrived (a date or timestamp); now when omitted.

notes.description: A free note on this receive, up to 1000 characters.

MerchantReceivePurchaseOrderRequest.title: Receive purchase order input

MetafieldDefinitionRequest.description:
Create/update/delete a metafield definition on the REST developer surface.

Over the Merchant API a key changes or deletes only its OWN installation fields
(owner type `installation`, PATCH|DELETE metafield-definitions/{definition}); the
merchant's and other apps' definitions answer 404 there.

`namespace`, `key`, `owner_type` and `type` are immutable after creation: a
stored value denormalises all four, so changing one would silently orphan
every value already written against it. Only presentation (`name`,
`description`) and `validations` may change, and a tightened validation is
documented as applying to future writes only.

The same rules back every surface that writes definitions, so all of them
accept exactly the same legal definitions.

merchant_access.description: What the merchant may do with the values of an app-owned definition: `read` or `read_write`.

MetafieldDefinitionRequest.title: Metafield definition input

p_id.description: Short, stable integer identifier of this object, the human-readable counterpart of its UUID.

app_owned.description:
True while an installation owns the definition (created in its own app_{slug}
namespace); false for the merchant's own, and after the app is uninstalled.

merchant_access.description: What the merchant may do with an app-owned definition's values: read or read_write.

created_at.description: When this object was created (ISO-8601 timestamp).

updated_at.description: When this object was last changed (ISO-8601 timestamp).

MetaobjectDataClass.description: What KIND of data a metaobject definition holds. `content` is merchant content (designers, size charts): entries may be storefront-visible and carry their own pages. `collected` is data gathered FROM people (form submissions, applications): entries are never storefront-readable and never revalidate the storefront. The booleans (`storefront_visible`, `has_pages`) stay the permanent source of truth — a collected definition is always stored with both off, however it is written.
MetaobjectDataClass.title: MetaobjectDataClass

MetaobjectDefinitionRequest.description:
Create/update a metaobject definition on the REST developer surface.

`type` is immutable after creation: entries carry it, and reference values
resolve through it, so changing one would silently orphan every entry and
link already written against it. The field SET may be replaced on update,
but removing a field (or retyping one) while entries still hold values for
it is a 422.

The same rules back every surface that writes definitions, so all of them
accept exactly the same legal types.

has_pages.description:
Whether entries of this type get their own public page at
`/{type}/{handle}`. A type matching a reserved storefront route
(cart, checkout, search and similar) is refused with a 422.

MetaobjectDefinitionRequest.title: Metaobject definition input

p_id.description: Short, stable integer identifier of this object, the human-readable counterpart of its UUID.

data_class.description:
The definition's data class (`content` or `collected`). Read-only
here: it is fixed at creation and cannot be changed through
this API.

app_owned.description:
True while an app installation owns the definition (its records
are the app's own data); false for merchant-held ones, including
a former app's after uninstall.

records_count.description:
How many entries a collected definition holds (null for content
definitions). Rendered on dashboard reads only, so store-key
responses never carry it.

created_at.description: When this object was created (ISO-8601 timestamp).

updated_at.description: When this object was last changed (ISO-8601 timestamp).

MetaobjectRequest.description:
Create/update a metaobject entry on the REST developer surface.

Shape is checked first (`type` exists, `handle` is slug-shaped, `status` is
known). Each field value is then validated against its definition — an
unknown key or a wrong-typed value fails with a `fields.{key}` error.
MetaobjectRequest.title: Metaobject input

currency.description: ISO-4217 currency code of the amounts on this object.
The market currency the shopper was charged in (ISO 4217).

unit_price.description: The unit price, add-ons included, in the market currency (a decimal string).

total.description: The line total in the market currency (a decimal string).

presentment.description: Market orders only: this in the market currency the shopper was charged in, beside the shop money above. Absent on every other order.

created_at.description: When this object was created (ISO-8601 timestamp).

properties.description:
Per-line checkout properties. Always present as an object so
dashboard chips and the shopper page never branch on absence.
Bearer keys are withheld here too (dashboard, shopper page,
rider): the order email is their only carrier.

property_labels.description: Declared line-text labels, `{property key: label}`, for the keys in `properties` an installed app declared on this product. Show those keys by label. Present only on the single-order read, and only when the line carries such a key.

payment_status.description: The stored word: `pending`, `unpaid`, `awaiting_confirmation`, `partially_paid`, `paid`, `overpaid`, `partially_refunded` or `refunded`; tolerate unknown words. Decide with `is_paid` / `is_payable`, never by comparing words.

is_paid.description: True when the money is in: `paid`, `overpaid` or `partially_refunded`.

is_payable.description: True when the order is open and still owes money (`pending`, `unpaid`, `awaiting_confirmation`, `partially_paid`).

channel.description:
`channel` is the messaging channel the order came through — never
the sales channel. The installed app source and caller reference
are exposed in the two keys below.

location_id.description: The number of the store location the order is fulfilled from (an order that names none is at the store's default location).

routing.description: Why the order is fulfilled from that location: `reason` (`default`, `only_location_with_all_items`, `first_location_with_all_items`, `most_stock_available`, `pos_device`, `manual`, `closest`), a plain `message`, and `short` (true when the location cannot cover every item).

custom_channel.description:
Import recognition: the sales channel that imported the order
(an app slug or legacy channel — null unless imported) and the
outside platform's own reference (null unless imported). Together with
`platform` (third_party) an app matches orders events to its
own records with no link table. Additive: both keys are null
for every order that is not an import.

publication.description:
Order attribution: the publication p_id the order was
imported through (null unless attributed). Readable by any
caller with order read scope — it discloses nothing new
beside custom_channel.

currency.description:
Vendor chain with the same unloaded-relation safety net as the
sibling order shapes: loaded relation first, then the
cache-backed lookup — never the silent platform default.

discount_total.description:
subtotal is the items BEFORE their automatic discounts, so those are part of discount_total, as is a delivery coupon (the fee
reads before it; delivery_fee is stored net): subtotal - discount_total + shipping_total + tax_total equals the total.

coupon_code.description:
The discount code the shopper entered at checkout, null when the order used none.
Additive and read-only: the code only, never the coupon's rules or usage.

shipping_total.description: The delivery or shipping fee charged for this order.

amount_paid.description: Recorded payments received minus refunds paid out, in `currency`.

balance_due.description: What is still owed while `is_payable` (total plus processing fee, minus `amount_paid`); `0` otherwise.

variant_id.description: The variant `p_id` the line was sold as (the `id` of `products/{product}/variants`), null for a product without variants or when that variant has since been deleted; match sales per variant on this, never on `variant_title`.

variant_uid.description: The variant UUID the line was sold as, kept even after the variant is deleted.

sku.description: The SKU of the variant sold, or of the product for a line without a variant; the store's current SKU, null when none is set or the variant was deleted.

refundable_quantity.description: How many of this line can still be refunded: the quantity less what earlier refunds took. `null` when the order's refunds were not read (a caller without merchant-orders-read, or a listing).

properties.description:
Per-line checkout properties (jsonb, array-cast). Absent lines
render an empty object, never null — apps always see the key.
An app's single-use keys (claims, manage links) reach only the
app that issued them, never another app or key.

metafields.description:
The receiver's own fields coming back to them: typed metafields the
merchant defined, and the opaque metadata an integrator wrote. This
is the whole point of order extensions — a webhook that omits the
ERP id forces the receiver to make a second call to match the order
to their own record.

QueekMetafieldType.description:
A metafield definition's `type`. Scalar forms, plus `list.<type>` for each listable one.

Limits (shared Postgres, part of the contract): 200 definitions per store, 50 values per resource, 65536 bytes per serialized value. Free-form `metadata`: 50 keys, key ≤ 64 chars, value ≤ 500 chars.

Reserved namespaces (a store may not define in these): `queek`.
Owner types wired in this version: `product`, `order`, `customer`, `collection`, `post`, `variant`, `installation`.

QueekWebhookTopic.description:
`orders/create` — An order was placed, on any channel.
`orders/paid` — An order moved to paid.
`orders/updated` — An order changed — status, fulfilment stage or any merchant action.
`orders/fulfilled` — An order was completed or delivered.
`orders/cancelled` — An order was cancelled or rejected.
`products/create` — A product was created in the store.
`products/update` — A product changed — visible content, price or availability.
`products/delete` — A product was deleted, soft-delete included.
`customers/create` — A customer record was created for the store.
`customers/update` — A customer profile field changed.
`customers/delete` — A customer was removed from the store, or lost the customer designation. This is a removal from the store's directory, not an erasure: data held elsewhere about that person is not deleted. The payload carries only the customer id.
`customers/data_request` — The merchant asked, on a shopper's behalf, for the data held about a customer. Delivered to every installed app that declares the topic, with no scope or consent line. The payload carries ids only: the request id, the customer id and the customer's order ids, never a name, email or phone.
`customers/redact` — The merchant asked, on a shopper's behalf, for a customer's personal data to be erased, and the cancellation window has passed. Delivered to every installed app that declares the topic, with no scope or consent line; the app erases what it holds about that customer in its own storage. The payload carries ids only: the request id, the customer id and the customer's order ids.
`customers_email_marketing_consent/update` — A customer email marketing preference changed.
`customers_marketing_consent/update` — A customer's SMS marketing consent changed.
`inventory_levels/update` — A product or variant stock level changed, with the reason.
`locales/create` — A locale was added to the store.
`locales/update` — A locale was published or unpublished on the store.
`locales/destroy` — A locale was removed from the store, with its translations.
`markets/create` — A market was defined on the store. It is created unpublished and changes nothing shoppers see or pay until it is published.
`markets/update` — A market on the store changed its name, countries or currency, or was published or unpublished. The payload is the market with its current `published` state.
`markets/destroy` — A market was removed from the store.
`translations/update` — Translations were registered on one resource, for the locales and keys in the payload.
`translations/delete` — Translations were removed from one resource, for the locales and keys in the payload.
`checkouts/create` — A signed-in customer's cart has been unchanged for the abandonment delay, reported for the first time. Fires when the idle delay passes, not when the cart is created or edited.
`checkouts/update` — A previously reported cart changed and has again been unchanged for the abandonment delay. Fires when the idle delay passes, not on every edit.
`payment_checkouts/create` — A signed-in customer's order has been left unpaid for the unpaid-checkout delay. Fires when the delay passes, not when the order is created; the payload is the same row `GET abandoned-checkouts?stage=payment` returns, with the order total and `recovery_url`, a payment link that does not expire (null for an order in a market whose exchange rate has expired) and is a secret. Needs both merchant-checkouts-read and merchant-checkouts-payments-read. Recovery is the `orders/create` webhook for the same order id (`order.id`): there is no update event, and an order paid, cancelled or followed by a later order before delivery sends nothing and is not retried. Delivery: sent once per unpaid checkout in normal operation; a delivery can occasionally be missed (infrastructure failure after the checkout is claimed) or arrive twice (retries): deduplicate by (topic, order id), and use GET abandoned-checkouts?stage=payment to reconcile.
`refunds/create` — A refund was recorded on an order: a credit to the customer's wallet, a refund to the original card or bank through the payment provider (it starts pending and ends success or failed, signalled by `orders/updated`), a refund the merchant recorded after refunding outside Queek, or a refund Queek pays the customer by hand because it could not be sent back automatically (type `manual`, starts pending).
`conversation_messages/create` — A shopper wrote a message in one of the store's messaging conversations. Fires once per message; the payload carries the conversation id, the channel and the message, and the rest of the conversation is read with the conversations API.
`invoices/create` — An invoice was created in the store's Invoices app: a draft, a duplicate, an invoice of an order, or a credit note (the note itself). The payload is the invoice `GET invoices/{invoice}` returns. Needs merchant-invoices-read, and the buyer's name, email and phone are null unless the installation also holds merchant-customers-contact-read. Nothing is sent when an order-backed invoice follows its order's payments: watch `orders/paid` and `refunds/create` for that. Apply each event as an upsert keyed by `data.id`: ignore it only when its `updated_at` is strictly older than the one you hold (two writes in the same second share a timestamp), and call GET invoices/{invoice} when unsure. A retry can send the same event again.
`invoices/update` — An invoice changed: edited, issued and numbered, voided, given a tax authority reference, had a payment recorded or voided, or was corrected by a credit note. The payload is the invoice `GET invoices/{invoice}` returns, with the same scope and contact rules as `invoices/create`. A change to an order-backed invoice that only follows its order's payments sends nothing (see `orders/paid` and `refunds/create`); an order cancelled with no payment voids its invoice with no event (watch `orders/cancelled`), and a customer's erasure or the store's deletion clears buyer fields with none (`customers/redact` is the signal). Apply each event as an upsert keyed by `data.id`: ignore it only when its `updated_at` is strictly older than the one you hold (two writes in the same second share a timestamp), and call GET invoices/{invoice} when unsure.
`invoices/delete` — A draft invoice was deleted (an issued invoice is voided, never deleted: that is `invoices/update`). The payload carries only the invoice id, the same `p_id` the invoice read answers.

RecordInvoicePaymentRequest.description:
Record money the merchant confirmed receiving. The amount is validated in the invoice's
own currency and precision; the date cannot be in the future. On the Merchant API the Idempotency-Key is
required (a retried call would otherwise record the money twice), checked with the permission, before validation;
the dashboard's own key stays optional.

amount.description: The amount received, a decimal above 0 in the invoice’s currency with no more decimals than that currency has. It may not exceed the balance left.

method.description: How the money arrived: `bank_transfer`, `cash`, `pos`, `mobile_money`, `other` or `tax_withheld` (tax withheld at source).

reference.description: Your reference for the payment, such as a transfer or receipt number, up to 120 characters.

paid_at.description: When the money was received. It cannot be in the future; defaults to now.

RefundOrderRequest.description:
POST orders/{order}/refunds, on the dashboard and the Merchant API: the one refund operation.

The gate order is the permission (the row's scope on the Merchant API), then the required
Idempotency-Key, all before validation. A dashboard SESSION that refunds money Queek holds (a wallet
credit or a provider refund) then confirms with the store transaction PIN, as a withdrawal does; a
refund that is only recorded needs none, and keys and apps act on their scope and the merchant's
consent. Where the money goes is never a field: it follows the original payment.

amount.description: How much to refund, a decimal string in the order currency with no more decimals than it has. Always sent: it is never computed from `line_items`. It may not exceed what is left to refund on the payment and on the order, and a refund through the payment provider cannot be below the provider's smallest (50.00 NGN).

payment.description: The payment to refund, a payment `id` from the order's `transactions`. Without it the newest received payment with something left is refunded; one request refunds one payment.

line_items.description: The lines refunded, so tracked stock can go back on the shelf (up to 100). They never set the amount.

order_item.description: The line, its `id` from the order's `line_items`.

quantity.description: How many of the line, 1 to the quantity not already refunded (`refundable_quantity`).

restock.description: Put the refunded quantity back in stock. Defaults to true; nothing is restocked for stock that was never taken (an order not completed, an untracked product).

notify.description: Tell the customer (a notice and an email) when the refund lands. Defaults to true; false sends neither.

reason.description: Why: `requested_by_customer`, `damaged`, `out_of_stock` or `other` (the default). For the store's records only.

note.description: A note for the store's own records (up to 500 characters). Never sent to the customer or in a webhook.

pin.description: The store transaction PIN. Asked of a dashboard session that refunds money Queek holds; ignored for API keys and apps.

RefundOrderRequest.title: Refund order input

transaction_id.description: The `id` of the payment that was refunded, as listed in the order's `transactions`.

type.description: Where the money went: `wallet_credit` (back to the customer's wallet), `original_payment` (back to the card or bank through the payment provider), `recorded` (the merchant refunded the customer outside Queek; Queek only records it) or `manual` (Queek could not send it back automatically and pays the customer by hand; `pending` until it does, and the store's share is taken back at once). Tolerate other values.

reason.description: Who started it: `order_cancelled` (the order was cancelled) or `merchant_refund` (the merchant or an app refunded it). Tolerate other values.

status.description: The refund's status; `success` once the money is back with the customer.

amount.description: The refunded amount, a decimal string in `currency`.

SendAppAlertRequest.description:
Send an in-app notice to the installing merchant from the calling
installation (POST app/alerts). The installation comes from the calling key
— the body carries no target, so one installation can never alert on another
installation's behalf.

Titles and messages are bell content by design: plain text, length-capped
like the manifest listing fields, rendered escaped on every surface. The
optional dedupe_key lets the app collapse repeats of one problem (one
failing import batch, one expired credential) inside the TTL.

option values ("Large / Red") by the variant service, as on every other writer.

StoreVendorInvoiceRequest.description:
Create a draft invoice (or proforma). Only what the merchant types is accepted; the
server computes subtotal, discount, tax and total and ignores anything else sent.

kind.description: The document type: `invoice` (a tax invoice, the default) or `proforma` (a quotation-style document that is not a tax invoice and takes no payment).

currency.description: ISO-4217 currency code of the amounts on this object.

customer_id.description: One of this store’s customers, by p_id or UUID. Their details fill the buyer; a `buyer` you send alongside overrides the fields it names. A customer that is not this store’s answers 422.

buyer.description: Who is billed: `name`, `email`, `phone`, `address` and `tax_id`, each optional. Omit it to bill the customer named by `customer_id`.

tax_id.description: The buyer’s tax registration number, printed on the invoice (up to 60 characters).

due_at.description: The payment due date (`Y-m-d` or an RFC 3339 timestamp). Null leaves the invoice with no due date.

terms.description: Payment terms printed on the invoice, up to 2000 characters.

note.description: A free-text note printed on the invoice, up to 2000 characters.

language.description: The language the document is rendered in: `en`, `fr` or `ar`. Defaults to the store’s invoice language.

discount.description: An invoice-level discount applied to the subtotal before tax: send `type` and `value` together.

type.description: How `value` is read: `fixed` (an amount in the invoice currency) or `percent` (0 to 100, up to 4 decimals).

value.description: The discount: a decimal amount at the invoice currency’s precision when `type` is `fixed`, a percentage from 0 to 100 when it is `percent`.

installments.description:
A payment plan: each instalment is a due date plus an amount, a percent of the total, or
(the last one only) nothing, which takes the remainder. The server makes them add up.

due_at.description: The date this instalment is due.

amount.description: The amount due in this instalment, a decimal in the invoice currency. Send this or `percent`; the last instalment may send neither and takes the remainder.

percent.description: The share of the invoice total due in this instalment, above 0 and up to 100 (up to 4 decimals). Send this or `amount`.

lines.description: The billed lines, 1 to 100. The server computes every line total, the tax and the invoice total from them.

quantity.description: How many units, above 0 and up to 1,000,000, with up to 4 decimals.

unit_price.description: The price of one unit, before tax, a decimal in the invoice currency with no more decimals than that currency has.

tax_rate.description: Absent = the store's own tax; a number, zero included, is the merchant's explicit rate.

tax_name.description: The name printed for this line’s tax (for example `VAT`), up to 80 characters.

taxes.description: Several named components on one line (Ghana: VAT, NHIL, GETFund); an empty list is an exemption.

rate.description: This tax component’s rate as a percentage from 0 to 100, up to 4 decimals.

required. `published` publishes or unpublishes: publishing answers 422 `market_publish_no_provider` or
`market_publish_no_rate` when it cannot be done yet.

name.description: The market's new name, unique within the store (1 to 100 characters).

countries.description: The full replacement list of countries, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes; a country belongs to one market of the store.

currency.description: The new currency (ISO 4217, not the store's own).

published.description: `true` publishes the market (422 `market_publish_no_provider` or `market_publish_no_rate` unless a provider can charge its currency and a current rate exists); `false` unpublishes it.

VendorOrderExtensionRequest.description:
PATCH orders/{order} — the developer-extension fields of an order, and
nothing else.

An order's state is NOT editable here: status, cancellation, rider
assignment and shipment each have their own endpoint with their own side
effects (stock, settlement, notifications, webhooks). Any field outside the
allowed set is rejected by name with a 422 rather than ignored — an
integrator who tries to cancel an order by PATCHing `status` learns it from
the error, not from an order that shipped anyway.

`metafields` must reference an existing definition for orders and never use
a platform (`app.*`, `queek.*`) namespace on this endpoint. `metadata` is
free-form integrator bookkeeping — replaced wholesale (`null` clears it),
capped in size and count, with no namespace rule and no definitions.
`line_items` merges per-line properties by key: an app mirrors what it
booked or issued onto the line it belongs to. Property keys from an app
installation key must live under its own `app.{slug}.` namespace; any other
caller writes any checkout-shaped key EXCEPT the app-owned `app.*` /
`queek.*` ones, so no merchant can forge or clear an app's keys. Keys and
values obey the documented caps.

key.description: Key of the custom field inside its namespace.

value.description: The value, typed by the field's definition. `null` clears the field.

metafields.description: Custom field values on this object, keyed `namespace.key`; `{}` when none.

metadata.description:
Free-form integrator bookkeeping: opaque strings in, the same
strings out. Never interpreted, never rendered — so the only rules
it can carry are size and count.

line_items.description:
Per-line properties to merge: a string sets the key, null
deletes it, keys you leave out keep their value.

id.description: The line item `id` exactly as the order object's `line_items[].id` carries it.

properties.description:
Key → value map merged into the line's `properties`. Keys are
`namespace.key` (lowercase, at most 64 characters); a line holds
at most 20 keys and the whole order 200, counted after the merge.

QueekLegacyErrorKeys.description: Additive legacy-compatibility top-level keys the runtime still emits on error bodies — never a replacement for `error.*`, which is the contract. `error_code` and `message` ride top-level on the refusals the platform itself raises; `request_id` and `doc_url` ride top-level ONLY on storefront, client, developer and dashboard error bodies — merchant routes reissue refusals, so there they live inside `error` and the `X-Request-Id` header. Some bodies keep their own top-level keys with `error` added beside them. Not referenced by any operation response: new integrations switch on `error.code`.

error_code.description: Top-level mirror of `error.code` on the refusals the platform itself raises (including the storefront sign-in branches).

message.description: Top-level mirror of `error.message` on the same refusals as `error_code`.

request_id.description: Top-level mirror of `error.request_id` ONLY on storefront, client, developer and dashboard error bodies. Always a string when present.

doc_url.description: Top-level mirror of `error.doc_url`, present on the same bodies as top-level `request_id`.
