post.description:
A signed-in customer's order has been left unpaid for the unpaid-checkout delay. Fires when the delay passes, not when the order is created; the payload is the same row `GET abandoned-checkouts?stage=payment` returns, with the order total and `recovery_url`, a payment link that does not expire (null for an order in a market whose exchange rate has expired) and is a secret. Needs both merchant-checkouts-read and merchant-checkouts-payments-read. Recovery is the `orders/create` webhook for the same order id (`order.id`): there is no update event, and an order paid, cancelled or followed by a later order before delivery sends nothing and is not retried. Delivery: sent once per unpaid checkout in normal operation; a delivery can occasionally be missed (infrastructure failure after the checkout is claimed) or arrive twice (retries): deduplicate by (topic, order id), and use GET abandoned-checkouts?stage=payment to reconcile.

Delivered to every active merchant-owned endpoint of the store subscribed to this topic, and to every app installation that is active, subscribed and holds all of the scopes merchant-checkouts-read and merchant-checkouts-payments-read. Endpoint subscriptions live outside this API (dashboard); verify the signature, dedupe on the event `id`, acknowledge with a 2xx inside 5s, and do the work asynchronously.

200.description: Acknowledged. Any other status (or a timeout) is retried on the published backoff schedule.

post.description:
An invoice was created in the store's Invoices app: a draft, a duplicate, an invoice of an order, or a credit note (the note itself). The payload is the invoice `GET invoices/{invoice}` returns. Needs merchant-invoices-read, and the buyer's name, email and phone are null unless the installation also holds merchant-customers-contact-read. Nothing is sent when an order-backed invoice follows its order's payments: watch `orders/paid` and `refunds/create` for that. Apply each event as an upsert keyed by `data.id`: ignore it only when its `updated_at` is strictly older than the one you hold (two writes in the same second share a timestamp), and call GET invoices/{invoice} when unsure. A retry can send the same event again.

Delivered to every active merchant-owned endpoint of the store subscribed to this topic, and to every app installation that is active, subscribed and holds the scope merchant-invoices-read. Endpoint subscriptions live outside this API (dashboard); verify the signature, dedupe on the event `id`, acknowledge with a 2xx inside 5s, and do the work asynchronously.

200.description: Acknowledged. Any other status (or a timeout) is retried on the published backoff schedule.

post.description:
An invoice changed: edited, issued and numbered, voided, given a tax authority reference, had a payment recorded or voided, or was corrected by a credit note. The payload is the invoice `GET invoices/{invoice}` returns, with the same scope and contact rules as `invoices/create`. A change to an order-backed invoice that only follows its order's payments sends nothing (see `orders/paid` and `refunds/create`); an order cancelled with no payment voids its invoice with no event (watch `orders/cancelled`), and a customer's erasure or the store's deletion clears buyer fields with none (`customers/redact` is the signal). Apply each event as an upsert keyed by `data.id`: ignore it only when its `updated_at` is strictly older than the one you hold (two writes in the same second share a timestamp), and call GET invoices/{invoice} when unsure.

Delivered to every active merchant-owned endpoint of the store subscribed to this topic, and to every app installation that is active, subscribed and holds the scope merchant-invoices-read. Endpoint subscriptions live outside this API (dashboard); verify the signature, dedupe on the event `id`, acknowledge with a 2xx inside 5s, and do the work asynchronously.

Apply each event as an upsert keyed by `data.id`: ignore it only when its `updated_at` is strictly older than the one you hold (two writes in the same second share a timestamp), and call GET invoices/{invoice} when unsure. A retry can send the same event again.
topics.invoices/update: An invoice changed: edited, issued and numbered, voided, given a tax authority reference, had a payment recorded or voided, or was corrected by a credit note. The payload is the invoice `GET invoices/{invoice}` returns, with the same scope and contact rules as `invoices/create`. A change to an order-backed invoice that only follows its order's payments sends nothing (see `orders/paid` and `refunds/create`); an order cancelled with no payment voids its invoice with no event (watch `orders/cancelled`), and a customer's erasure or the store's deletion clears buyer fields with none (`customers/redact` is the signal). Apply each event as an upsert keyed by `data.id`: ignore it only when its `updated_at` is strictly older than the one you hold (two writes in the same second share a timestamp), and call GET invoices/{invoice} when unsure.
topics.invoices/delete: A draft invoice was deleted (an issued invoice is voided, never deleted: that is `invoices/update`). The payload carries only the invoice id, the same `p_id` the invoice read answers.
